prompt: Explain the primary function of GPIO pins on an ESP32 microcontroller. Then, provide a short, conceptual explanation of how you would configure one of these pins to read the state of a physical push-button.
rawOutput:
The primary function of GPIO (General‑Purpose Input/Output) pins on an ESP32 is to provide digital interfaces that can be programmed as either inputs (to sense voltage changes from sensors or switches) or outputs (to drive signals to other devices). Each pin can be configured by software to detect a specific logic level, making the microcontroller able to interact with a wide range of digital hardware.

To read the state of a push‑button with one GPIO pin, you would first connect the button’s two terminals to two pins (or to one pin and a ground reference). Then, in the code, declare the pin as an input (e.g., using pin_mode(pin, INPUT)) and, in the main loop, call a digital‑read function such as digital_read(pin). The read will return a HIGH or LOW value while the button is pressed, allowing you to determine whether the button is being held down. If a pull‑up or pull‑down resistor is added, the pin will default to a known state when no button is pressed.
